exposure: low-dose spinal anesthesia (1.8 ml 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine)
0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine (low dose - 1.8ml vs conventional dose - 2.2ml)
conventional-dose spinal anesthesia (2.2 ml 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine)
outcome: Pain (measured using a visual analog scale)
cohort: 70 healthy parturients undergoing elective cesarean section
finding: Low-dose spinal anesthesia provided similar hemodynamic and analgesic effects compared to the conventional dose for cesarean section.
mod_finding: This study compared two different doses of hyperbaric bupivacaine for spinal anesthesia during cesarean sections and found that a lower dose had similar analgesic and hemodynamic effects as a conventional dose, but with faster recovery.
